13291.html:
13291 *savēla 'in time, early'. [Semant. cf. sakāla-, *savāra-. — sa-², vḗlā-]
    S. savera f. 'an early hour', adj. 'early' = savero (forms with -l-, savela f., savelo ← L.); L. savēl, °lē adv. 'early', awāṇ. savēl, °lā adj., °lē 'in the morning', poṭh. savelā 'good'; P. savel, saver f. 'morning, dawn', savelā, saverā 'early, in good time', °le, °re adv.; Ku. N. saber 'early in the morning' (-b- < emph. -vv- or more prob. from simplex ber); H. sawerā m. 'early morning'; G. saveḷā, saverā adv., M. saver (a lw. ac. to LM 416, but see vḗlā-).

poṭh. savelā 'good'; P. savel , saver f. 'morning, dawn', savelā , saverā 'early, in good time', °le , °re adv.; Ku. N. saber 'early in the morning' (- b - < emph. - vv - or
more prob. from simplex ber ); H. sawerā m. 'early
morning'; G. saveḷā , saverā adv., M. saver (a lw. ac. to
LM 416, but see vḗlā- ).

13533.html:
13533 *suvēlā 'good time'. [su-², vḗlā-]
    K. sul, sulᷴ f. 'good time, early time, early dawn, spare time', suli adv. 'early, at dawn'; M. suveḷ f. 'auspicious period, favourable time (in general)'.
    Addenda: suvitá-: WPah.kṭg. sv́i, kc. sve f. 'woman's greeting to men and elder women'.

6328.html:
6328 dina n. 'day' Mn. (in cmpds. in RV.). [√dī³]
    Pa. dina- n. 'day', Pk. diṇa- n.m.; K. dĕn m. 'day, daytime', ḍoḍ. dinā̃ obl. pl.; S. ḍ̠iṇu m. 'festival day, present sent to married daughter on such a day'; L.awāṇ. diṇvār 'festival' (vāra-²: prob. L. cmpd., but cf. dinavāra- m. 'weekday' Gaṇit.); N. din (dinahũ, dinũ 'daily'); A. din 'day', dinā 'daytime', dinīyā 'equal to a day'; B. Mth. Aw.lakh. H. din m. 'day, daytime' (→ P. WPah.paṅ. cam. din m. or, like G. M. din, ← Sk.), OG. diṇa n.
    daina-; dinakara-; madhyáṁdina-.
